title: Go: Loops
description: Use Go's only loop keyword — for — in various forms: basic, while-style, range, break, and continue.

steps.title: Basic For Loop
steps.description: Write a for loop that prints numbers 1 to 5, each on a new line.
hints: Go uses `i++` not `++i` as a statement.
No parentheses around the three components.

verification.failureMessage: Print numbers 1 through 5 using a for loop.

steps.title: For as While
steps.description: Use a for loop as a while loop to print numbers 1 to 5.
hints: Omit the init and post statements.

verification.failureMessage: Print 1 to 5 using for as a while loop.

steps.title: For Range Over Slice
steps.description: Create a slice `fruits := []string{"apple", "banana", "cherry"}` and use `for range` to print each fruit.
hints: You can ignore the index with `_`.

verification.failureMessage: Print each fruit using for range over the slice.

steps.title: Break
steps.description: Write an infinite loop `for { ... }` that breaks when `i` reaches 5, printing each value of `i`.
hints: `for i := 1; ; i++ { if i > 5 { break }; fmt.Println(i) }`
Or use `for { ... }` with a condition inside.
Break exits the innermost loop immediately.

verification.failureMessage: Print 1 to 5 using an infinite loop with break.

steps.title: Continue
steps.description: Print even numbers from 1 to 10 using a for loop with `continue`.
hints: `for i := 1; i <= 10; i++ { if i%2 != 0 { continue }; fmt.Println(i) }`
